questions.q: Why is inserting, deleting, or reordering columns on an FBDI template considered one of the most damaging mistakes?
options: It makes the Excel file larger in size
It breaks the direct mapping between spreadsheet columns and interface-table columns, silently, with no warning from the macro
It changes the font used in the template
It has no real effect on the import
questions.explain: Column position is how the template's macro maps spreadsheet values to interface-table columns. Changing that mapping produces no warning, just wrong data landing in wrong columns.

questions.q: What problem can occur if leftover sample or placeholder rows are not deleted from a template?
options: The file becomes automatically read-only
They are automatically ignored with no effect
Excel refuses to open the file at all
They get exported as if they were real rows, causing duplicate or invalid data
questions.explain: Sample rows left in place are not automatically filtered out — they get generated into the CSV file and treated as real data by the import process.

questions.q: A supplier number '00452' is typed into a column formatted as a general number. What is the likely result?
options: The leading zeros are dropped, turning it into '452' — a different value
It stays exactly as '00452'
Excel automatically converts it to a date
The entire row is deleted automatically
questions.explain: Numeric-formatted cells typically drop leading zeros, which can change a supplier number into a completely different value.

questions.q: Why can a file with structural or data-entry mistakes still upload successfully to UCM and load into an interface table?
options: Because UCM rejects every file with any mistake, so this situation cannot occur
Because Oracle automatically fixes all mistakes during upload
Because those steps only check that the file is a well-formed CSV, not whether its business content makes sense
Because the interface table does not actually exist
questions.explain: Upload and interface-table loading check file format, not business rules. Business-rule validation only happens later, during the product-specific import process.

questions.q: Which of these belongs on a pre-flight checklist BEFORE generating CSV files from a template?
options: Deleting the Instructions tab
Confirming no columns were added, removed, or reordered, and that lookup fields use codes rather than labels
Renaming every column header to something more descriptive
Converting all dates to text so they display as typed
questions.explain: A pre-flight check confirms the template's structure and data are intact: correct columns, correct tab, codes instead of labels, consistent dates, and no stray rows.
